classifiedFinding.justification: Fork-confirmed and a genuine footgun (a competent owner would not expect a 0.001-phUSD swap to split the cutover with no resume), so it is reported, not suppressed. But the impact it unlocks is custody of protocol POL on the trusted OWNER's own EOA plus a liveness stall that the owner can unwind by hand: in A the owner holds both legs and can seed the pair directly (the plan, BalancerWinddownPlan.md L414, already anticipates 'recovered sUSDS and phUSD sit on OWNER ... operator re-runs from step 6'); in B the owner holds the BPT and can exit it directly, and a proportional recovery exit remains available after 30 Nov (plan L22/L38). ECON-001 shows zero extractable value, so no Medium value-leak path exists. The availability impact is narrower than it looks: index-4 minting keeps working after 30 Oct because BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch never calls Balancer (plan L9), so only pool() and the cutover schedule are affected. Decisively, the vulnerable sequence has no mainnet entry point at a4f9f3c (story 103 is incomplete; the core is called only by DeployMocks), and story 103 is specified to move it onto the atomic escrow. Case for Medium (recorded): fork-proven, cheap/organic trigger, ~$41k, violates story 103's 2026-10-07 'no protocol funds transit the owner EOA' requirement, opens the 9a694ae01fe1 poisoning window, and the deadline compresses recovery time. Case for Low (chosen): no loss, trusted custodian, manual recovery available, not yet broadcastable, matches run-31..37 precedent of 0 H/M for pre-broadcast cutover tooling with borderline cases held at Low. Faithfulness facet (EOA custody vs the 2026-10-07 amendment) is tagged but carried by DEDUP-008/DEDUP-009 rather than a separate F label.

finding.variantDecision: Scenario B kept in this finding (same root cause). Both scenarios end with protocol value on the OWNER EOA mid-sequence and no resume; the defect enabling both is step 4 moving BPT to the EOA in a separate tx with no idempotent gates. One mitigation (atomic escrow exitAndSeed, or core resume gates + floor-based seeding) closes both. B differs only in which leg of the stall holds the value (BPT vs pool tokens).
finding.description: Under forge --broadcast, steps 4, 5 and 6 are separate OWNER transactions whose amounts are baked in simulation. A Balancer swap that lands before the step-5 exit either (A) shifts the per-BPT composition inside the 1% _checkMinAmountsOut window so the exit succeeds but the baked step-6 addLiquidity pulls more of the short leg than OWNER holds (0 spare sUSDS, 1.47 phUSD), or (B) pushes the exit past its floor so it reverts after step 4 already moved all BPT to OWNER. Either way ~$41.3k of protocol POL sits on the OWNER EOA, which story 103's 2026-10-07 requirement ('no protocol funds transit the owner EOA') forbids. The canonical pair stays empty and public, which extends the ledgered 2-wei poisoning window (9a694ae01fe1), and index 4/hook remain on the old pooler. Re-running the core fails at step 5 (bptIn == 0) or step 0.
finding.economicAnalysis: ECON-001: zero extractable value. The seed either lands at exactly the simulation price or the short-leg transferFrom reverts, so the core can never seed at a manipulated ratio. The attacker's round trip loses ~2 x 0.3% fee (-0.60 sUSDS at 100, -1.11 at 185.7, -11.2 at 2,000). Pure grief at <$0.20/attempt. The 1% tolerance (~$206.6/leg) is a revert bound, not a loss bound (refutes MR-002's 'up to 1% extractable').
finding.impact: Liveness + custody: protocol liquidity stranded on an EOA until a hand-written recovery; new pair left exposed to the 2-wei poisoning brick meanwhile. No third-party theft path (owner controls the EOA, Law 3).
finding.attackVector: Organic: the pool saw 5 swaps in the last ~7 days. Adversarial: watch the mempool for OWNER's removeLiquidityProportional and front-run it with a dust swap in either direction. This is the same ~$0.03 trigger as ycn L-28. Here the exit SUCCEEDS (it stays inside the floors) and the seed reverts. Under a --slow Ledger broadcast forge then halts. State: ~18,572 sUSDS + ~22,559 phUSD (live share of 20,401.8 BPT) sit on the OWNER EOA, which is exactly what story 103's 2026-10-07 'no funds through any EOA' requirement forbids. UniPoolerV2 is deployed but unseeded, the canonical pair exists and is empty and public (poisonable, see 9a694ae01fe1), and index 4/hook are still on the old pooler. There is no resume entry point: re-running _runCutover fails step 5 (bptIn == 0, L374). Without --slow, steps 7-12 would still land after the failed seed and cut index 4 over to an UNSEEDED pooler.
finding.recommendation: Wire story 103 onto UniPoolerCutoverEscrow.exitAndSeed (atomic, whole-balance seed). Until then, do not broadcast the core in PROPORTIONAL mode. If it is kept, seed desired = the on-chain-guaranteed minAmountsOut floors (not simulation deltas), sweep the remainder later, and add per-step skip-if-done gates.

finding.description: The helper gates liquidity on the canonical pair EXISTING, not on it having reserves. Story 111 deploys the helper BEFORE the cutover. The pair exists from cutover step 1 onward, and earlier if anyone calls the permissionless factory.createPair. Any addLiquidity through the helper while the pair is still empty makes that caller the first LP and gives the pair non-zero reserves. That permanently fails core step 2 (L339/344) and the escrow's PairNotEmpty, and UniPoolerV2's canonical-pair constructor check means no alternative pair can be used. finding.title: Cutover core's 'read live' rescue amounts and post-conditions (mintDebt==0, old pooler drained, _assertRetired) run only in forge simulation; interim index-4 mints before step 10 leave unswept sUSDS on the paused old pooler, and a re-enabled donation could revert the step-11 USDS rescue
finding.rootCause: ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast: amounts read in simulation are baked into calldata; every require between external calls is simulation-only, while index 4 still dispatches to the old pooler until step 10 is mined.
finding.description: The 'read live after step 10' amounts are read in simulation and baked into the rescue calldata. The drain checks at L532-535 and in _assertRetired run only in simulation. Until the step-10 tx is mined, index 4 still dispatches to the old pooler, and every interim mint wraps USDS into sUSDS ON the old pooler (BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch). That sUSDS is not covered by the baked rescue. It stays on the old pooler after step 12 pauses it. The mint rate since the 2026-10-01 holding pattern is ~1,957 sUSDS in ~12 days. Conditional brick: if the owner re-enables the donation on the old pooler before the cutover (live batchDonationSize is 0, so this does NOT apply to today's config), an interim mint's PSM sweep consumes the parked USDS. The on-chain balance can then fall below the baked usdsRescued, so the step-11 USDS rescue reverts. The broadcast halts before step 12, leaving the old pooler unpaused with NFTMinterV2 still its minter. PATTERN-003 adds: the step-7 mintDebt==0 check and the step-4/5/6 baked bal/bptIn/sAmt/pAmt are the same simulation-only mechanism (the step-5/6 facet is carried by DEDUP-001 and not double-counted here).

finding.impact: No loss: rescueERC20 is onlyOwner and not pause-gated, so residue is recoverable (opportunity cost per ECON Q4). Retired pooler silently keeps protocol sUSDS that in-script post-conditions claim is zero; conditional step-11 revert (only if donation re-enabled; live batchDonationSize = 0) halts before step 12.
finding.recommendation: Run step-11 rescue in a second invocation after step 10 is mined, or have story 103's verify assert old-pooler sUSDS/USDS == 0 and mintDebt == 0 live after broadcast and sweep residue.

finding.rootCause: Step 9's new-pooler setters sit between the hook repoint and the dispatcher swap, and the core has no skip-if-done gates (step 0 requires hook.dispatcher == oldPooler).
finding.description: After step 8's setDispatcher lands, BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook.onDispatch reverts OnlyDispatcher for the old pooler (hook L109-110). ATokenDispatcherV2.dispatch calls hook.onDispatch unconditionally, so every index-4 mint reverts until step 10 is mined. In between sit setHook plus the step-9 setters: setMinter, setPSM, setMaxTout, setBatchMinter, setBatchDonationSize, setAuthorizedPooler x4 and setNudgeStreamer, about 11 Ledger-signed --slow transactions. The window is inherent to three independent owner contracts. The real hazard is that the core is not resumable. If the broadcast halts anywhere in steps 8-10 (Ledger timeout, gas, nonce), index 4 stays bricked, and re-running _runCutover fails step 0 L297 (hook.dispatcher != oldPooler). Story 103 says 'resume from receipts', but the core has no skip-if-done gates to resume through.
finding.impact: Index-4 mints revert (user keeps USDS, loses gas; no fund loss per ECON Q4) for the window, indefinitely if the run halts inside it.
finding.recommendation: Move step 9's configuration before step 8 (it touches only the new pooler) so steps 8-10 are three consecutive transactions. Give story 103 per-step idempotent gates (as StableStakerCutoverCore did after L-02 2c82d65e65e1), or disable index 4 in NFTMinterV2 across the window.

classifiedFinding.justification: The RECOVERY branch is broken as written, and test_cutover_recovery proves a property that does not hold on mainnet because MockBalancerVault treats paused as recovery-allowed. That is a real Law-2 / test-fidelity defect on the plan's deadline fallback. The fork result that enableRecoveryMode reverts SenderNotAllowed for OWNER is from the LIVE pool, which is the expected authorized-only behaviour pre-pause. It does not show that the fallback is dead. The plan (L21, L34, L38) says Balancer enables Recovery Mode where needed, and that enableRecoveryMode is permissionless once paused, so the remedy is one permissionless call before re-running the script. The failure is caught in forge simulation before any tx, including step 4's withdrawBPT, is broadcast, so it fails closed with nothing stranded. That keeps it at Low rather than raising it. finding.rootCause: Price drift since plan block 26,093,540 (holding pattern stopped pool() 2026-10-01).
finding.description: The seed price carried over by the proportional exit is 0.8233 sUSDS = $0.9160 per phUSD. For a 50/50 weighted pool, the token-unit balance ratio equals the spot price, so the V2 seed reproduces the Balancer spot exactly, as plan decision 3 intends. The seed is 8.4% below the $1 mint price. Minting is mint-only (no redemption floor), so a below-peg seed opens NO mint/sell arbitrage. Back-running the seed has no edge either: the V2 pair and the Balancer remnant start at the identical price. Since the plan's block 26,093,540, the price has fallen from 0.971 to 0.916 (the holding pattern stopped pool() on 2026-10-01). The live crossing Delta* on the seeded pair is 1,895 USDS, against the plan's ~$640 and F-03-052's $1,712. Using the stale figure for the 'first call about Delta*' errs SAFE (undershoot, no arb skim). Pooling the whole post-cutover sUSDS balance at once (1,957.66 sUSDS = 2,178 USDS) overshoots by ~$283, lifts phUSD to ~$1.0125, and costs about $0.2 of arb skim (~141 phUSD minted, which is collateral the no-ceiling design wants). Negligible.
finding.impact: None material. The stale numbers err in the safe direction.
